assumption: People want an after-training bar that is high in protein, low in sugar AND made from real food
current_evidence: PARTLY SUPPORTED (8 Oct): 7/10 positive about the concept; 4/10 value whole foods or object to 'bad ingredients' (C1 C2 C4 C7); 4/10 focus on protein (C1 C3 C5 C10); S&C coach advises whole foods (E1). BUT 0/10 commitments - interest is not demand
cheapest_test: Ask every interviewee for a waitlist sign-up or taste-test slot; post the landing page
metric: % of interviewees who commit; waitlist sign-ups
success_threshold: >=50% of interviewees commit; >=150 sign-ups by Week 12

assumption: Bars taste and feel good enough to eat repeatedly (v6: eggs, quark, oats, oat bran, seeds; little or no honey)
current_evidence: RISK RAISED: taste is a concern for 3/10 (C3 C8 C9); coach (E1) puts texture and taste first and saw students struggle to eat squad-supplied Grenade bars
cheapest_test: Blind taste test: v6 vs v5 vs Grenade/Warrior RAW (n~20)

assumption: People will pay ~£2.75 for a 90 g fresh bake
current_evidence: RISK RAISED: price is a concern for 3/10 (C1 too expensive; C5 price important; C6 priced out); Warrior RAW sells at ~£1/bar with 20 g protein
cheapest_test: Waitlist price question + pilot price test (£2.25 vs £2.75 at different partners)

assumption: Coached athletes (primary persona) need it most and their coach can open the squad channel
current_evidence: SUPPORTED (small n): athletes 2/3 whole foods, 2/3 protein, 2/3 can't cook (C1 C7 C10); E1 influences squad nutrition. All 3 athletes male
cheapest_test: Ask E1 for a squad taste test; interview 3 female athletes
metric: Squad agrees to pilot; female athletes describe same need

cheapest_test: Paid pilot at 2 partners over 3 weeks

assumption: ~16-17 g protein (high protein by law, 25% energy) is enough
current_evidence: MIXED: legally 'high protein' now; 4/10 protein-focused; professor (E2) suggests ~10 g protein per 100 kcal (v6 = 6.2; lab bars 8.4-10.5)
cheapest_test: Pilot survey: 'Would you want more protein even if it meant protein powder?'

assumption: A chilled product with a ~3-day use-by works for partners
cheapest_test: Ask partners in pilot chats; count waste
metric: Partners with fridge; % of bars wasted

assumption: Calculated numbers hold in a real bake (v6 hero: 1.9 g sugar, 16.7 g protein, 25% energy from protein, 90 g)
current_evidence: Calculation; 30% bake loss assumed; claim margins: sugar 2.1-3.9 g/100 g vs 5 limit; protein ~25% vs 20% limit
cheapest_test: Weigh before/after baking + 1 lab nutrition analysis

assumption: Home-baked bars are consistent bake to bake
cheapest_test: Weigh 8 bars from each of 3 bakes

assumption: Use-by of at least 3 days agreed with the EHO
cheapest_test: Fridge keep test days 1/3/5/7 + ask EHO

assumption: Some buyers prefer a smaller bar (half-bar, 45 g)
current_evidence: C5 chooses Fulfil partly for size
cheapest_test: Offer halves in the taste test and pilot

assumption: 'fettle' is free to use as a trade mark in classes 29/30
current_evidence: No clash found by web search; UK IPO not checked
cheapest_test: UK IPO + Companies House search (30 min)

assumption: A local bakery could bake it under contract at <=£0.95/bar
'High protein', 'low sugar' and 'kitchen ingredients' wording is acceptable to Trading Standards
current_evidence: Claims checked vs GB register conditions

assumption: T20 keeps acceptable quality chilled for 3+ days and survives freezing/thawing; athletes will order weekly to fit a short shelf life
current_evidence: UNTESTED (8 Oct): moist baked egg/dairy bar (~40% water, calculated) needs chilling; Simmer Eats runs a 5-day chilled model (C40); freezing egg bakes ~2-3 months (S22, weak)
cheapest_test: Home fridge sensory test day 1/2/3/5; freeze 3 bars and thaw at 1/2/4 weeks; ask interviewees if they would order a weekly box
metric: Day-3 and thawed taste scores vs fresh; % who would order weekly
success_threshold: Day-3 and thawed scores within 1 point of fresh; >=50% would order weekly
